Title: NS polls: Anwar shocked by attacks against Anthony Loke during campaigning
Article:
JELEBU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he was shocked by the relentless attacks against DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke during the Negri Sembilan election campaign.
He described Loke as as an honest and hardworking leader.
He said Loke was being unfairly targeted despite having a proven record in government and questioned the motives behind attempts to discredit him.
"I was surprised. Every day they attack Loke. In other places, everything is blamed on Anwar. But here in Negri Sembilan, everything is Loke's fault.
"What kind of people are they? Did he steal money? Did he grab land? Did he take projects? Is he lazy? Hasn't he performed well as a minister?"
Anwar was speaking at the "Majlis Minum Petang Bersama PMX" programme in Simpang Durian.
Loke, who is contesting the Chennah seat under Pakatan Harapan, also attended the event.
Anwar attributed the attacks to jealousy and an attempt to replace a leader with a strong track record with those whose records were weaker.
The PH chairman also rejected attempts to identify Loke solely based on his ethnicity, saying leaders should be judged by their integrity, competence and commitment to serving Malaysians.
"If I want to choose an Orang Asli representative, I choose the best one. If I choose a Malay leader, I choose someone who is trustworthy, not someone who abuses power.
"The same goes for Chinese leaders. I choose the one who is more capable, more trustworthy and who works for the people."
Anwar said he had worked alongside Loke for decades and had witnessed his commitment since his early days in the Reformasi movement.
"I did not get to know him only this year. We have struggled together for decades. When I first fought for Reformasi, he had just graduated from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia and joined the movement.
"At that time, neither of us knew we would one day become ministers (together), but we continued the struggle because we believed in bringing change," he said.
Anwar described Loke as a Malaysian leader who consistently supported policies benefiting all communities.
"Whenever I spoke about strengthening Islam, improving education for Malays, hostels or assistance for Mara, he never once objected.
"He also speaks up for Orang Asli, Malays and the Chinese community. That is what a Malaysian leader does," he said.
He urged voters to support Loke, saying the transport minister had demonstrated integrity and dedication in serving both the government and the people.
"Loke may be Chinese, but he is a Malaysian leader who is respected and plays an important role in this country. Support him," he said

Title: Ringgit edges higher against greenback as investors await FOMC outcome
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed marginally higher against the US dollar on Wednesday as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of the outcome of the United States Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) meeting.
At 6pm, the local currency appreciated to 4.0875/0915 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0885/0930.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit remained largely range-bound against the US dollar, and other Asian currencies showed similar trends, as traders and investors awaited the FOMC's decision later tonight.
"The US dollar could receive a boost should the Federal Reserve adopt a hawkish tone, as elevated crude oil prices may suggest that the decline in the June inflation rate is temporary," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said developments in West Asia remained fluid following reports that the US military had intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles launched at its forces, with global crude oil prices subsequently rising.
"West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude oil prices rose by 3.67 per cent and 3.79 per cent to US$82.17 per barrel and US$87.28 per barrel, respectively," he said.
The ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies at the close.
It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.4982/5008 from 2.4948/4976, depreciated vis-à-vis the euro to 4.6561/6606 from 4.6429/6480, and declined versus the British pound to 5.4351/4405 from 5.4287/4347 on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, the ringgit also traded lower against regional currencies.
It weakened against the Indonesian rupiah to 226.1/226.5 from 226.0/226.4, declined versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1632/1666 from 3.1603/1640, shed vis-à-vis the Thai baht to 12.1971/2138 from 12.1494/1681, and slid against the Philippine peso to 6.65/6.67 from 6.63/6.64 yesterday.

Title: Police developing system to track repeat traffic offenders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) is developing a data system to track repeat traffic offences, including drink-driving cases detected under Op Mabuk.
Its director, Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali, said the system would help the department keep track of traffic offenders' records, including whether the offence was their first, second or third violation.
He said tracking repeat traffic offences remains a challenge as they were not recorded the same way criminal records are maintained by the Criminal Investigation Department.
"TEID is developing a data system for repeat offence records. At present, only the courts maintain these records.
"The records will only cover offences under traffic laws," he said at a press conference in Bukit Aman today.
Hasbullah said the system was important to allow authorities to trace people who had been arrested or punished for traffic offences.
"We face challenges because past traffic offences were not comprehensively recorded.
"We need a new system so that we can check an offender's record, including how many times they have offended."
On driving under the influence offences, Hasbullah said despite intensified operations, many people were still being detained for the offence.
He said this showed that road users' awareness remain low.
"Road crashes were increasing, so we intensified operations. When we increased operations, we found that many people still had low awareness.
"We will propose that the Transport Ministry and the Attorney-General's Chambers review the penalties because people are not learning their lesson."

Title: Regime change? Inside Reza Pahlavi's faltering bid to lead Iran
Article:
AS the US and Israel went to war on Iran this year, a transformative moment seemed to have arrived for Reza Pahlavi, son of the autocratic shah who was overthrown in 1979.
Despite not having set foot in Iran in almost half a century, Pahlavi had been actively campaigning in the US and Europe, giving speeches about a bright new future for his homeland, raising money and meeting elected officials.
"The Iranian people have called on me to lead the transition after the regime is gone," he declared on the social-media platform X shortly after the war began in late February.
"I have accepted that responsibility."
In Texas this March, Pahlavi received one of the most enthusiastic receptions at the Conservative Political Action Conference.
As he took the stage, staunch supporters of President Donald Trump and a large contingent of Iranian Americans, many draped in the pre-revolution Iranian flag that flew during his father's rule, lavished him with a 45-second standing ovation.
Four days later, Trump horrified many Iranian emigres by declaring in a social-media post: "we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!"
To the shock of some of Pahlavi's Iranian-American financial supporters – one of whom said the donors had recently given his campaign more than US$3 million in the hope he could lead a new, transitional government in Iran – the exiled prince didn't swiftly condemn Trump's remarks.
Now, Pahlavi's triumphant appearance at CPAC appears to mark the apex of his rise as the most visible candidate vying to step in should the hardline Islamic government fall.
Although he continues to campaign, his candidacy has sputtered. In mid-January, Trump told Reuters that Pahlavi "seems very nice, but I don't know how he'd play within his own country."
And behind the scenes his administration sidelined the prince.
As Iranian-American human rights activist Ahmad Batebi prepared to address a Jan 15 United Nations Security Council meeting on Teheran's bloody crackdown on protests earlier that month, US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz personally urged him not to mention Pahlavi by name, according to two people familiar with the exchange.
Although Batebi supports Pahlavi, he complied.
[[nid:1499795]]
In a statement, Waltz told Reuters he suggested "a tight focus" on Batebi's own experience of torture in Iranian prisons and "the barbarism of the regime" would make "the greatest impact, rather than opposition politics."
In June, the tattered ceasefire pact signed by the US and Iran made no mention of regime change. Instead, the US agreed to respect Iran's sovereignty and refrain from interfering in its internal affairs — and publicly dismissed Pahlavi again.
"The President of the United States never said that his goal was to install Reza Pahlavi to become the new leader of Iran," US Vice President JD Vance told podcaster Megyn Kelly after Trump announced the US-Iran memorandum of understanding on June 14.
Pahlavi and his top aides were left to blast the agreement on social media.
Meanwhile, some of Pahlavi's financial backers, who communicate in a private WhatsApp group, have grown disillusioned not just by his muted criticism of Trump's extreme wartime threats.
In private calls, according to three people familiar with the matter, Pahlavi listened to but ultimately ignored their advice to try harder to unify the opposition and to forcefully condemn some of his more radical supporters' violence against and harassment of other Iranian dissidents.
There is no evidence that Pahlavi had anything to do with those incidents.
Pahlavi's faltering leadership bid highlights one of the major flaws in the US-Israeli war on Iran: the lack of a clear alternative to the Islamic Republic.
Shortly after the bombing began in late February, Trump called for the Iranian people to rise up and take over their government.
But despite an air strike that killed the Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the government has survived the onslaught — and in the view of many Iran watchers, has tightened its hold on power.
'I'M A BRIDGE TO THE DESTINATION'
In two interviews with Reuters this month, including a lengthy video sit-down in Paris, Pahlavi stressed that Iran's current government is "very close" to collapse.
"This campaign started as a lifetime mission to liberate Iran 46 years ago," he said. "And it has never been about me. It's been about the Iranian people and their right to self-determination."
His role, he said, is to lead a transition to a new democratic government: "I'm not the destination, I'm a bridge to the destination."
While Pahlavi's supporters see him as a unifier, several attempts he was involved in to unite the long-divided opposition collapsed.
In one case in 2023, three people familiar with the matter say, his wife insulted other opposition leaders, which she denies.
Two activists also say he was mostly all talk and no action during a campaign to designate as a terrorist organisation the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which wields vast military, political and economic power in Iran.
For this story, Reuters interviewed more than 50 people, including eight of Pahlavi's current and former associates; reviewed hundreds of pages of legal documents; and sifted through extensive video, photographic and social-media records of Pahlavi and his supporters, some of whom favour a restoration of Iran's pre-revolutionary monarchy.
Pahlavi's main credential is being the son of the last shah of Iran.
Unlike many successful revolutionaries of the recent past, such as South Africa's Nelson Mandela, Poland's Lech Walesa or the Islamists who overthrew his father, Pahlavi doesn't seem to have a mass organised movement inside the country ready to roll into power.
Far from a sputtering campaign, Pahlavi described a robust "mobilisation to overcome this regime" and told Reuters it's "not true" that he hasn't built a mass movement.
Huge numbers of Iranians heeded his call to protest in the streets on Jan 8 and 9, he said, and many died when the government responded with gunfire.
He said he communicates with "cell leaders" of "over a thousand different groupings" that span labour, academia, religion and ethnic organisations "to be ready to intervene the moment that we have that opening."
Reuters was unable to independently confirm how many groups inside Iran are working with him. It was Teheran's "massacre" of demonstrators in January that Pahlavi said changed his view on foreign intervention.
That month, an Iranian official told Reuters that deaths in street protests had reached at least 5,000; Pahlavi puts the figure at 40,000.
[[nid:1499794]]
The Iranian people are still the "boots on the ground," he said, but they need foreign military help to "equal the playing field."
He said he hasn't sought the endorsement of any government or leader: "It is not for a foreign government to decide who or what should be the alternative for Iran. That's up to the Iranian people."
In the interviews, Pahlavi did not directly address Trump's post about blasting Iran back to the Stone Ages but stressed, as he has in the past, that military strikes should "hit the regime as hard as you can" but spare "civilian infrastructure."
Speaking about his own movement, Pahlavi unequivocally condemned violence by his more radical supporters and said he has worked hard to unify the Iranian opposition, gathering together representatives "from all walks of life, ideologies.
"In fact, I've reached out to people who were, at the time, my father's worst enemies. Today, they are fully on board working with me."
Pahlavi said his critics "are entitled to their opinion. Some people may not like my face. Some people may think that I should be doing this and that," he said. But, he added, "I think for the most part, I'm enjoying a lot of support across the board, inside and outside of Iran."
Some of that support, he acknowledged, comes from his family legacy: "Yes, I happen to have the Pahlavi name. And by the way, that's a positive. That's what people are chanting on the streets."
While it's difficult to obtain accurate polling in an authoritarian society, a survey of 31,450 Iranians late last month found that about 48 per cent view Pahlavi favourably, according to Ammar Maleki, director of the Netherlands-based Gamaan Research Institute, which conducts online polling in Iran.
'ROYALIST BUBBLE'
It has been 48 years since Pahlavi, the eldest son of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, was in Iran.
An aviation enthusiast, he moved to Texas in 1978 at age 17 to begin jet pilot training at Reese Air Force Base.
After the 1979 revolution – which began as a broad-based uprising against his father's repressive rule but produced the Islamic theocracy – he remained abroad, earning a bachelor's degree from the University of Southern California in social sciences and communication.
His life in exile has been marked by repeated personal tragedy. His father died in 1980 from complications related to non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
His younger sister, Leila, died in London in 2001 of a drug overdose. His brother Alireza, a doctoral student in ancient Iranian studies at Harvard University, took his own life in 2011.
Pahlavi, 65, has never held a conventional salaried job, according to three people who have known him for years.
Instead, he has spent his years in exile as a political activist, casting himself as leading the Iranian opposition and accompanied by a rotating set of supporters, some of whom have turned against him.
"If an attorney decides to take a case pro bono, does this mean that he doesn't have a job?" Pahlavi told Reuters. "I've been doing this voluntarily for free for four decades as my sacrifice for the sake of my country."
[[nid:1499793]]
US Representative Derrick Van Orden, a Wisconsin Republican who met Pahlavi in his Washington office in May, said he found him articulate and humble.
"He's tall, and you know, he just looks presidential."
Van Orden said he challenged Pahlavi over the "despicable" conduct of SAVAK, the shah's secret police, telling him "not everybody has the best memory of your father's rule, and he acknowledged it."
Others have been less impressed. Ali Vaez, Iran project director at the International Crisis Group, a conflict-prevention organisation, said that after meeting Pahlavi 15 years ago, he concluded he lacked the appetite for the political rough-and-tumble needed to lead change in Iran.
"Talking to him, you realise he's much more passionate about football, food and photography than politics," Vaez said.
"It was, and still is, abundantly clear that he doesn't have what it takes to be a leader."
Scott Anderson, author of "King of Kings: The Iranian Revolution," a 2025 book about the uprising that toppled Pahlavi's father, said, "He's lived in this kind of royalist bubble."
Anderson added, "Everything I've always heard about him from people in the Iranian diaspora is that he's kind of a lightweight."
In response, Pahlavi said: "I could have easily decided back in Cairo when my father passed away, 'You know what? To hell with it. I can pursue, like many others, a life, business, other things.'"
Instead, he said, "I decided to stay in it for the sake of my country."
Anderson and other experts do agree that Pahlavi is the most widely recognised Iranian opposition figure.
The opposition in Iran, a nation of more than 90 million, encompasses monarchists, socialists and Marxists, republicans, and a range of secular, religious and ethnic blocs.
While they share opposition to the Islamic Republic, they often disagree fiercely over what and who should replace it.
Citing the shah's authoritarian legacy, some of those opposition groups question whether Pahlavi would adhere to his stated plan to oversee a transitional government and then let Iranians choose their future system.
Asked if he would rule out becoming monarch even if the Iranian people were to vote for a constitutional monarchy, Pahlavi told Reuters:
"Well, I'm telling you, I am not running for office. That has never been my preoccupation. And it also depends on, at the end, what it is that best serves the country's purpose."
Nostalgia for the stability and relative prosperity that some Iranians enjoyed during his father's rule has burnished his image over time.
Nahid Khazraee, 54, left Iran when she was 16. She was among the protesters who marched through New York City on May 16 in support of Pahlavi.
She wore a locket with images of Trump and Pahlavi, which she said symbolized "MIGA" – Make Iran Great Again.
Pahlavi, she told Reuters, "is the only person that everyone would trust, because our grandparents, our family, they all used to have good days [before the] revolution happened."
KICKING AND PUNCHING
Dilovan Emadaldin Silashor thought he was going to die.
[[nid:1499792]]
On March 9, the Kurdish freelance reporter from Iraq was covering the aftermath of a fight that had broken out after Pahlavi supporters turned up at a Kurdish restaurant in London and demanded the establishment display Iran's pre-revolution lion-and-sun flag, a symbol of support for the shah's son.
Iran's Kurdish minority is estimated to comprise between about 10 and 17 per cent of the population.
Moments after Silashor arrived, he said an Iranian man shouted abuse at a group of local Kurds standing guard outside the restaurant, sparking another confrontation.
As Silashor filmed, several Iranian men turned on him, knocking him to the ground and repeatedly kicking and punching him in the head and back, he said. He put his satchel over his head to protect himself.
"This is the end of my life," Silashor recalled thinking. He was treated in a hospital later that night for extensive bruising of his ribs and said he continues to suffer back and leg pain.
After reporting the assault to police, Silashor said officers showed him photographs from which he identified one of his alleged attackers.
Reuters reviewed that man's social media accounts, which contain numerous posts showing him attending pro-Pahlavi demonstrations and rallies. Many display the lion-and-sun flag.
The man denied attacking Silashor in an online message to Reuters, saying, "I did not hit that boy at all." Police said they are still investigating after they arrested two men and released them without charges.
The assault was one of at least four recent incidents across three countries – the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Austria – in which Reuters documented Pahlavi supporters engaging in violence or harassment.
In addition, two Pahlavi supporters were charged in March in Canada with the murder of a Pahlavi critic.
Addressing violence by his supporters, Pahlavi told Reuters: "I condemn it. I distance myself from that. I don't justify it. I don't condone it. And, in fact, I ask for whatever authority it is to have them face the crime they've committed. You cannot just go and start brutalising people."
A BUNCH OF "NOBODIES
According to some of Pahlavi's critics, he has failed to tamp down the abusive rhetoric that some of his closest aides, as well as his wife, have levelled against other Iranian dissidents, further dividing an already fractious opposition.
In early 2023, opposition figures launched a unity effort that came to be known as the Georgetown Coalition after the university in Washington, D.C, where it first convened.
As part of that effort, members gathered in Toronto in March 2023 for a panel discussion.
As attendees waited in a side room to take the stage, Yasmine Pahlavi, the exiled prince's wife of 40 years, entered and, unprompted, told the other dissidents they were "nobodies" compared to her husband, according to three people familiar with the exchange.
The remark stunned those present. Among them was Hamed Esmaeilion, whose wife and daughter were killed when Iran's IRGC shot down a Ukraine International Airlines passenger jet in 2020.
Also present was the Iranian-American journalist and political dissident Masih Alinejad, who had been the target of an assassination attempt. Within weeks, amid disagreements over the group's direction, the coalition disbanded.
In a statement to Reuters, Yasmine said she never made the remark, calling it a "complete fabrication. No such interaction occurred in Toronto. Such lies are disappointing."
Others in the prince's inner circle have also been accused of launching divisive attacks on Pahlavi's opponents.
One key aide, Saeed Ghasseminejad, wrote in a January post on X: "You're either with Prince Reza Pahlavi or with the Islamic Republic. If you're weakening the field commander for any reason whatsoever, you're an agent of the enemy."
Ghasseminejad told Reuters the tweet addressed "a small extremist faction of the monarchist movement" that he said was attacking Pahlavi for insisting on a referendum to decide the form of Iran's future government.
Hossein Ronaghi, an Iran-based dissident who has been jailed multiple times by Iranian authorities, told Reuters he has been smeared repeatedly by Pahlavi supporters.
He said he doesn't hold Pahlavi responsible for the attacks, "but he does bear a political and moral responsibility to speak out clearly, repeatedly and unequivocally against threats, intimidation, fabricated accusations and the exclusion of opponents."
Pahlavi said he has spoken to his close aides about some of their rhetoric and is establishing "a much stricter protocol" for them: "You can no longer act independently. You have to be much more careful."
A DEATH FORETOLD
On March 6, police found the corpse of Masood Masjoody, an Iranian-born academic and math tutor who lived near Vancouver. Soon after, authorities charged two Pahlavi supporters with murdering him.
Masjoody was a dedicated pro-democracy Iranian activist who had previously supported Pahlavi, even engaging in a lengthy video conversation with him in 2021.
He also had ties to two of Pahlavi's closest aides, Ghasseminejad and Amir Etemadi; they all attended Tehran University at around the same time, according to a person who knew them.
The three men later became active members of a pro-Pahlavi political group, the Iranian Liberal Students and Graduates.
Masjoody and Etemadi also joined the Iran Revival Network, or Farashgard, which also supported the prince. Ghasseminejad confirmed he attended university with Masjoody but said he had not been in touch with him for a few years. Etemadi did not respond to requests for comment.
But Masjoody ultimately broke with Pahlavi. In 2024, he filed a series of lawsuits in British Columbia's Supreme Court against Pahlavi and some of his supporters, ultimately comprising thousands of pages of court documents.
"Through his office, advisors, secretaries, and associates, Pahlavi has an ongoing history of directing cyberattacks on dissenting Iranian activists, particularly the pro-democracy ones," one of the lawsuits alleged.
Masjoody argued that Pahlavi was "vicariously liable for the conduct of his supporters," who he said were "acting under his influence."
[[nid:1499791]]
Pahlavi initially didn't respond to two lawsuits against him. But after learning that Masjoody had obtained default judgments against him, Pahlavi filed two sworn affidavits in November 2025 in which he denied Masjoody's allegations.
In both of his affidavits he stated: "I do not know the plaintiff Masood Masjoody." The two men had met online, though.
In July 2021, Masjoody participated in a private video call over Zoom with Pahlavi and two other activists, according to a person familiar with the call.
Masjoody recorded it and later posted to YouTube the portion of the call where he and Pahlavi interact. In addition, Saeid Hosseinpour, who was active in Farashgard, said Masjoody was on some of the many Zoom calls that group members had with Pahlavi.
Pahlavi told Reuters he has held Zoom calls with thousands of people. "I really do not recall having had any specific conversation with this individual," he said.
By late last year, Masjoody became convinced that two "die-hard loyalists to Reza Pahlavi," whom he had also sued, were plotting to assassinate him.
In October, he claimed on X that the alleged plotters – Mehdi Ahmadzadeh Razavi and Arezou Soltani – had sought to obtain a lethal substance to kill him in order to halt the lawsuits he had lodged against Pahlavi and others.
Rosita Fatemi, a local doctor, later submitted an affidavit stating she had met with the two alleged conspirators in September 2025 and one of them "asked me for a drug substance to 'get rid of him.'
"Based on the context of the discussion, I understood to be referring to and causing him to be murdered." Fatemi said she refused the request.
Several of Masjoody's friends told Reuters he sent them messages that he requested they pass on to the police if he was murdered. One of the messages included mention of his Zoom call with Pahlavi.
In early February, Masjoody was reported missing by neighbours. The next month, after his body was found, the pair Masjoody had accused of plotting to kill him were charged with first-degree murder.
Attorneys for the two suspects didn't respond to requests for comment on the case. The accused remain in custody.
There is no indication Pahlavi was involved in any way. "This is tragic," he told Reuters. "Whoever was responsible for this murder ought to be facing a court of law and be judged for the crime they've committed."
The cases brought by Masjoody have effectively halted, with a judge in Vancouver ruling that defense applications to dismiss them "are moot as a result of his death."
'PAHLAVI BOYCOTTED US'
The Islamic Republic's main instrument of repression and power abroad is the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Pahlavi has repeatedly tweeted his support for designating the group a terrorist organisation, which would bar it from banking and doing business with Western firms.
"For at least the last 10 years," he told Reuters, "I've been one of the first advocates of proscribing the IRGC as a terrorist organisation."
But two activists involved in a global campaign to get nations to brand the Guards as terrorists say that other than social-media posts and at least one newspaper opinion piece, Pahlavi was largely absent.
Alireza Akhondi, an Iranian-born member of Sweden's parliament, was a leader of the effort. He said he met Pahlavi twice in 2023 to ask for his support as the campaign organised demonstrations in Strasbourg, France, and later Brussels.
He said he asked Pahlavi to sign a statement that would be published in European and US newspapers to demonstrate support from a wide range of Iranian opposition groups, and to attend the Brussels rally or at least send his daughter.
"You can own this campaign if you want," Akhondi said he told Pahlavi. "He said he would get back to me with an answer" after one of the meetings, Akhondi recalled. "He didn't."
Hassan Verkiany, who worked on the campaign in a different role, said: "Reza Pahlavi boycotted us" and "avoided participating in all events associated with the IRGC campaign."
In response, Pahlavi told Reuters that sometimes activists "would like to utilise you in a way to boost their own personal campaign as opposed to a general cause." He added, "I think this is perhaps what is the issue."
[[nid:1499790]]
In January, the European Union finally designated the IRGC a terrorist group, as the US had done in 2019. Pahlavi tweeted: "I welcome the EU's decision to designate the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corp (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation."
A TRILLION-DOLLAR GROUP CHAT
After the Israelis bombed Iran in last year's 12-day war, 15 leading Iranian-American business people launched a WhatsApp group to discuss the situation privately.
It eventually grew to 28 members. The companies they lead, said one member, currently have a combined market cap of more than US$1 trillion.
In January, after thousands of demonstrators in Iran reportedly were calling out Pahlavi's name, members of the WhatsApp group discussed supporting him financially.
Not everyone was enthusiastic. "They didn't have the conviction that this is the right guy," said one member of the group. In the end, fewer than 10 contributed a total of more than US$3 million, this person said.
Among the donors was Dara Khosrowshahi, Uber's chief executive, whose family fled Iran just before the 1979 revolution. A company spokesman confirmed that the CEO made a contribution, but said he isn't a monarchist and primarily pitched in to help pay for Pahlavi's security.
The spokesman said Khosrowshahi agreed to contribute because he understands that Pahlavi only intends to serve as a transitional figure in introducing democracy in Iran.
To boost Pahlavi's profile, another donor arranged for him to meet Jamie Dimon, the CEO of JPMorgan Chase. A bank spokesman confirmed the meeting but declined to discuss the conversation.
A third donor, Hamid Moghadam, executive chairman of real-estate logistics giant Prologis, travelled to Washington in early February and met with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
"I wanted to hear the views of an Iranian-American who cares deeply about democracy and prosperity for the Iranian people," Moghadam told Reuters.
He said he mentioned Pahlavi as a potential path to democracy in the hope that the Trump Administration would engage with him. Rubio listened but made no commitment, Moghadam said.
Pahlavi told Reuters he had only recently begun soliciting large contributions.
In the past, he said, most of his funding came from small donations, "without a single penny coming from any outside public or government funds." Reuters wasn't able to independently confirm all the sources of his funding.
Cameron Khansarinia, Pahlavi's chief of staff, said the funds primarily go to security, travel, payroll, media projects and planning for the transition to a new government.
One Iranian-American donor said it was assumed that Pahlavi would pay more attention to the advice of his financial backers. But despite frequent video calls between Pahlavi and some of the business people, "that proved not to be the case."
The donor hasn't contributed more. "We're all business people. You want to have a return on investment."
In response, Pahlavi said, "I'm not going to change the mission based on the benefactor's expectation that I pay you, but you have to do X, Y and Z. That's not the way it works."
Now, with the war heating back up, Pahlavi faces a more critical test of his leadership than dealing with disappointed donors.
He told Reuters that he knew the ceasefire "is not going to last." When it came out, he denounced "deals and compromises with a criminal regime." Last week, he told Reuters that the Iranian people shouldn't be used as "pawns" in "any kind of negotiation.
The people did not get killed for purposes of keeping the Hormuz Strait open or to achieve a nuclear deal. They died for freedom and liberty."
For decades, he has insisted that to achieve democracy the Islamic Republic must fall.
But even amid a renewed wave of conflict that has killed at least four US soldiers and wounded many others, the Trump administration continues to negotiate with Iran's theocratic government.
And Washington is not demanding what Pahlavi needs most: regime change.
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: From messaging to intelligent engagement: Lessons from a decade in Malaysia
Article:
THE last decade of customer engagement in Malaysia has proven that digital reach is merely a foundation, not a finish line.
Businesses wanted to send alerts, open service channels, launch apps and make themselves easier to contact.
That work mattered. It helped bring more customers into digital journeys and made everyday services more accessible.
But the market has moved on. At the start of 2025, Malaysia had 34.9 million internet users, equivalent to 97.7 per cent of the population.
In a market this connected, being reachable online is no longer enough.
Customers now expect digital engagement to be immediate, useful and capable of helping them complete what they came to do.
The most significant shift in consumer behavior is that communication and service have become inseparable.
Customers now perceive any message that fails to facilitate immediate action as inherently incomplete.
When Reliability Becomes Trust
This shift is most apparent during service disruptions, such as payment failures, flight changes, or broadband outages.
In these critical moments, customers stop caring about the underlying mechanics of channels, systems, or automation.
Instead, they demand clarity on what went wrong, actionable steps for resolution, and assurance that the business will take ownership once the automated process reaches its limit.
This is why reliability has become part of customer experience.
In Malaysia, digital services are now woven into daily life, from banking and payments to deliveries, appointments and service requests.
When one fails, the issue is no longer only technical downtime. It becomes a test of trust.
Bank Negara Malaysia's penalties against four banking institutions after prolonged disruptions in 2024 underline how resilience in essential digital services has become a governance and customer-trust issue.
Conversational AI does not prevent a core-system outage. But it can shape how customers experience one.
Properly integrated, it can provide verified updates, explain what is affected, surface the right next step and route sensitive cases to a person without forcing the customer to start again.
The value is not a more polished chatbot. It is a system that can connect to operational information, act where appropriate and transfer context when human judgement is needed.
This principle is equally vital in routine service journeys, as demonstrated by Telekom Malaysia Bhd's efforts to unify email, WhatsApp and social media interactions.
By ensuring that relevant customer history follows the conversation, the company resolves everyday requests more efficiently and prevents every interaction from becoming an isolated, repetitive case.
Why Intelligence Needs Memory
This requirement for unified context extends naturally to AI.
As Malaysia's digital landscape matures - marked by the launch of the National AI Office - enterprises must ensure that AI doesn't simply add another layer of complexity.
The challenge is not just to integrate AI, but to avoid adding another silo.
Many organisations underestimate the significant risk of fragmented technology.
While individual tools for customer service, marketing, and analytics may be effective in isolation, their failure to share context creates a disjointed experience for the customer.
This lack of integration leads to frustrating outcomes, such as receiving marketing promotions while an issue remains unresolved, being forced to repeat information or encountering automated responses that completely miss the mark.
This is why AI orchestration is essential; it integrates customer data, communication channels, AI agent's and next-best actions into a unified system.
By aligning these elements, businesses can intelligently determine the appropriate response, trigger the right capability, and identify the precise moment for human intervention.
That is the logic behind Infobip AgentOS. It brings AI agents, journey orchestration, channels, customer data and human intervention into one coordinated layer.
The aim is not to automate every interaction. It is to make routine journeys faster while ensuring complex, sensitive or high-value moments reach the right person with the relevant history intact.
That history matters because personalisation is also changing.
Customers are less impressed by how much a business knows about them than by whether that knowledge makes the next interaction easier.
Helpful personalisation reduces uncertainty, effort and repetition.
Invasive personalisation makes assumptions, surfaces irrelevant offers or uses customer information without a clear benefit.
AirAsia's timely travel communications show how useful relevance can be when itinerary information matters most.
Maybank Philippines reflects the same lesson in a more regulated setting: in financial services, relevance must sit alongside speed, simplicity and security.
The foundation for this is customer memory. Not memory in the intrusive sense, but the practical ability to understand what has already happened, what the customer currently needs and ensure that relevant context transitions seamlessly into every future interaction.
That requires more than campaign data or a basic CRM record.
It requires a customer data platform that can unify and resolve behavioural, transactional and conversational signals into a usable profile.
A Conversational CDP provides this critical foundation for Infobip AgentOS, equipping both AI agents and human teams with the context needed to make superior decisions and ensure that the right information is seamlessly shared during a human handover.
The point is not to know everything about a customer but to apply the right information responsibly.
By doing so, every interaction becomes less repetitive, more relevant, and consistently more considered.
Next Decade Will Be Defined By Judgement
This is becoming more important as business communication enters its next phase.
Infobip's Messaging Trends Report 2026 found that total conversational interactions grew 25 per cent, while chatbot interactions on its platform increased 40-fold over five years.
AI is moving beyond experimentation and into the operating fabric of customer engagement.
That does not make trust less important. It makes it the central discipline.
Malaysia's initial 10 years of digital interaction centered on accessibility: onboarding consumers, diversifying touchpoints and establishing widespread connection.
The coming era will hinge on discernment - the ability to deploy intelligent systems with the necessary perspective and oversight to foster genuine dependability in every brand-customer partnership.
The companies that lead will not simply place more technology between themselves and their customers.
They will use it to make service faster when it should be, more considered when it needs to be, and more human when it matters most.

Title: Reforms start delivering results, says Bank Negara governor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's structural reforms are beginning to pay off, strengthening the economy's fundamentals, attracting higher-quality investments and lifting investor confidence, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said.
Rasheed said while structural reforms typically take time to bear fruit, their impact is increasingly visible through investment policies, fiscal measures and improvements in administrative efficiency.
"Malaysia recorded its highest-ever investment approvals of around RM431 billion last year, compared with RM384 billion in 2024.
"More importantly, these investments are of higher quality, particularly in sectors such as semiconductors, memory chips and integrated circuits," he told BuletinTV3 at Bank Negara headquarters today.
Rasheed said investor confidence had also improved, supported by the National Investment Aspirations and Malaysia's efforts to attract investments into strategic, higher-value sectors.
The strength of investor appetite was also evident in Malaysia's latest global sukuk issuance, which attracted demand of nearly five times the US$1.5 billion offered last week.
On the fiscal front, Rasheed said the government has implemented measures to optimise public spending, including targeted subsidies, while maximising national revenue.
As a result, Malaysia's fiscal deficit narrowed to 3.7 per cent last year, compared with 6.4 per cent in 2021, he said.
"These structural changes are something we must continuously pursue to enhance competitiveness.
"Looking ahead, our focus will be on two key areas: structural reforms in the labour market and strengthening social protection for the people," he said.
Rasheed explained that labour market reforms aim to create more high-quality, high-income jobs while upgrading the skills of the local workforce to meet the needs of higher value-added industries.
On social protection, he said government assistance, including support for education, should be better targeted toward those who genuinely need it.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ipoh Sungai Pari Flats block to be demolished after deaths
Article:
IPOH: The abandoned 15-storey Sungai Pari Flats block, where two schoolgirls were found dead last week after allegedly falling from the building, will be demolished as part of a redevelopment project.
Perak Housing and Property Board (LPHP) chief executive officer Zaiteena Wan Nasir said LPHP had appointed a developer to redevelop the site.
"The land belongs to LPHP and we have appointed a developer to undertake the redevelopment.
"Based on the current plan, two heritage buildings will be retained while the remaining buildings, including the 15-storey block, will be demolished and replaced with new developments," she said.
She said this at a press conference after attending the Perak Bumiputera Property Aspiration Programme at a hotel here.
The event was launched by Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.
Zaiteena said demolition works would not begin immediately as the developer must first obtain planning permission from the Ipoh City Council (MBI) and secure rezoning approval.
"That process will take some time. The developer must also install safety hoarding around the site before any demolition works can commence," she said.
She said the appointed developer would decide whether to undertake the demolition works in-house or appoint another contractor.
"We have handed over the site to the developer. Decisions on when the demolition will take place, who will carry it out and the demolition method are entirely up to the developer, who will also bear the costs.
"The developer will ensure all necessary safety measures are in place before work begins," she said.
Zaiteena said the redevelopment could only proceed after an issue involving ownership of a temple within the project site was resolved.
Meanwhile, Saarani said every aspect of the redevelopment must comply with legal requirements while taking into account the interests of all stakeholders.
Last Friday, two 14-year-old
schoolgirls were found dead
after they were believed to have fallen from an upper floor of the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats.
The Sungai Pari Flats, also known as 'Sungai Pari Tower' or 'Tingkat 15', was once an iconic landmark in Ipoh, famed for its bowl-shaped rooftop design and status as the city's tallest building.
The public housing project, built in 1963, was gradually vacated from 2012 following concerns over its structural condition.

Title: Econpile wins RM39mil subcontract for bored piling, substructure works
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Econpile Holdings Bhd has been awarded a subcontract worth RM39.52 million from WCT Construction Sdn Bhd to undertake the earthworks, bored piling and substructure works here at Jalan Awan Besar in Mukim Petaling.
Its wholly owned subsidiary, Econpile (M) Sdn Bhd, received the letter of award for the proposed commercial development consisting of four blocks of five-storey commercial shop units, comprising 68 units, two levels of sub-basement car park, and one commercial unit, one main switch station and one refuse chamber.
The project is expected to be completed within 15 months from July 29, 2026 onwards. It will contribute positively to the company's revenue from the financial year ending June 30, 2027 onwards.
"There are no foreseeable significant risks other than operational risk associated with the project during the contract period.
"The management would put in place control measures and operational procedures to reduce the impact or likelihood of such events," said the civil engineering company in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
It also noted that none of the directors or major shareholders of the company or persons connected to them have any interest, whether direct or indirect, in the project.

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: No hiding for those responsible over TH losses
Article:
JELEBU: Those responsible for losses and abuse of power involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) must face investigations and prosecution if there is sufficient evidence.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the cabinet's decision to declassify and release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH also included directing enforcement agencies to act on any criminal wrongdoing uncovered.
"The decision today was not only to release the report. Those responsible for losses, fraud and abuse of power will be investigated by the police, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), Bank Negara Malaysia and under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
"If there is evidence, they will be charged and, if found guilty, sent to prison. That is how the rule of law works," he said in a speech at the "Majlis Minum Petang Bersama PMX" programme in Simpang Durian.
Anwar said TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain had briefed the cabinet earlier in the day on the RCI's findings, which showed the pilgrimage fund had suffered losses amounting to RM10 billion.
He said the losses stemmed from investments that failed to comply with regulations and poor governance practices dating back to 2014.
He said Bank Negara had written to TH in 2014 warning of regulatory breaches, but the concerns were allegedly ignored, eventually contributing to the financial losses.
"The losses occurred because procedures were not followed, investments were made improperly and there were many governance issues," he said.
Anwar said the government's priority was to safeguard public institutions and ensure that the savings of Malaysian pilgrims were protected.
"I only want to ensure this country remains prosperous and free from corruption and abuse. I am not the one conducting the investigations or handing down punishments.
"The police investigate, MACC investigates corruption, the Attorney General decides on prosecution and the courts determine guilt," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Experts back proposal for dedicated Maritime Court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Establishing a dedicated Maritime Court would significantly improve legal certainty, enhance Malaysia's standing as a regional maritime legal hub, and strengthen investor confidence in the shipping sector, experts said.
Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia Faculty of Syariah and Law International Law Unit head researcher Assoc Prof Dr Mohd Hazmi Mohd Rusli said that while the High Court currently exercises admiralty jurisdiction competently, the highly technical nature of maritime disputes warrants a specialised judicial tribunal.
"Maritime disputes are highly specialised, often involving complex issues such as ship financing, cargo claims, marine insurance, and cross-border enforcement," he told the New Straits Times.
"A dedicated Maritime Court would improve consistency, efficiency, and legal certainty. It would also strengthen Malaysia's reputation as a maritime nation and enhance confidence among international shipping stakeholders, aligning with national aspirations."
He was responding to
Transport Minister Anthony Loke, who said the Admiralty Bill was aimed at creating a dedicated maritime court
.
"We will table the bill at the year-end parliamentary session. The bill will provide a source of power to establish a special court for maritime matters.
"At present, we do not have a dedicated maritime court. What we have is the High Court, with one of its courts specialising in maritime cases.
"The bill is to provide the source of power so we can establish a more comprehensive judicial system for handling maritime disputes and related issues," he said.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said on July 13 that the bill would be referred to a special select committee for further scrutiny before being debated in the Dewan Rakyat.
Hazmi said the vast majority of admiralty disputes in the country stem from commercial matters rather than environmental accidents.
"Common cases include ship arrests, cargo loss or damage, charterparty disputes, marine insurance claims, collisions, and disputes over ship ownership or mortgages.
"As a nation bordering vital maritime chokepoints, oil spills do occur, but they are relatively less common compared with commercial shipping disputes."
On legal capacity, he said Malaysia already had a capable pool of maritime lawyers, particularly in key economic areas such as Kuala Lumpur, Port Klang, Johor, and Penang.
Hazmi said establishing a specialised court would create increased demand for deeper expertise, presenting an opportunity for universities and the legal fraternity to strengthen both public and private maritime law education.
He added that Malaysia should position itself as a credible and cost-effective alternative to established maritime dispute venues such as Singapore, rather than attempting to directly replace them.
"Malaysia borders two of the busiest straits in the world, giving it significant importance in global trade. With its strategic location, major ports, and lower operating costs, Malaysia holds strong potential to become a preferred venue for maritime disputes if the bill is implemented effectively."
Hazmi also proposed that the court be supported by well-trained judges, modern case management technology, and clear admiralty laws aligned with international best practices, while continuing to function alongside existing maritime arbitration and mediation channels.
Lawyer Rajesh Nagarajan said replacing inherited United Kingdom laws with a domestic statute would give Malaysia full ownership of its maritime legal system.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zulkifli: RCI report provides opportunity to strengthen Tabung Haji governance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji presents an opportunity to strengthen the pilgrims fund's governance and should be viewed as a catalyst for further reforms rather than a setback for the institution.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the declassification of the report reflected the government's continued commitment to transparency, accountability and good governance.
He said Tabung Haji has served millions of Malaysian Muslims for more than six decades by managing haj savings and pilgrimage affairs, making it one of the country's most respected Islamic institutions and an internationally recognised model for Islamic fund management.
"The findings and recommendations of the RCI should be viewed positively as a valuable opportunity to further strengthen institutions such as Tabung Haji.
"Tabung Haji has been implementing the RCI's recommendations in a structured manner to safeguard the interests of depositors, ensure continued syariah compliance and strengthen the institution's long-term sustainability," he said in a statement today.
Zulkifli said the reforms have gone hand in hand with Tabung Haji's improving financial performance, demonstrating that the institution remains on a strong footing despite the challenges identified in the inquiry.
He added that Tabung Haji has continued to receive international recognition for its haj management, having consistently won the Diamond category of the Labbaytum Award presented by the Saudi government.
"The implementation of the RCI's recommendations and these achievements will serve as a catalyst for Tabung Haji to continue pursuing excellence, drive service innovation and deliver optimum returns for depositors."
Zulkifli said all religious agencies under the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) remain committed to supporting efforts to ensure Tabung Haji remains financially sustainable, retains the confidence of Malaysian Muslims and continues to lead the country's haj management.
Earlier today, the cabinet agreed to declassify and release the
RCI
report on Tabung Haji following a briefing by the institution's top management.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the report contained 25 recommendations, of which about 75 per cent had already been implemented by Tabung Haji.
The cabinet also directed enforcement agencies to immediately proceed with comprehensive investigations based on the report, with those found to have breached the law to be brought before the courts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: West Bank violence, annexation 'only getting worse': UN
Article:
GENEVA: Two years after the International Court of Justice said Israel's occupation of the West Bank was unlawful, settler violence and territorial annexation is "only getting worse", the UN said Wednesday.
The United Nations' human rights office said that with attacks by Israeli settlers and the creation of outposts "hitting an all-time high", countries had to act to end the occupation.
"We are alarmed by the Israeli government's announcement to further increase the number of settlements and outposts, and open calls by Israeli leaders for revenge and collective punishment against Palestinian communities, accompanied by threats to turn the West Bank into another Gaza," rights office spokeswoman Ravina Shamdasani said in a statement.
In a sweeping, non-binding "advisory opinion" issued in July 2024, the UN's top court said that Israel's decades-long occupation of Palestinian territory was "illegal."
Israel is "under the obligation to bring to an end its unlawful presence as rapidly as possible", presiding judge Nawaf Salam said.
Violence in the West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began with Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel.
The West Bank has seen near-daily attacks by Israeli settlers and regular raids on Palestinian villages.
Shamdasani said that since last Thursday, eight Palestinians, including a boy, as well as two members of the Israeli military had been killed in the West Bank, which has been occupied by Israel since 1967.
"Settlers and Israeli security forces, often acting together, have attacked local communities, assaulting families, destroying and confiscating property, and burning mosques," she said.
"Movement restrictions are now tighter, blocking Palestinians from reaching essential services."
Last Friday, deadly clashes broke out last between Israeli settlers and Palestinians in the village of Tell that left four Palestinians and two Israelis dead.
The Israeli military subsequently raided the city of Nablus and several nearby towns, announcing the arrest of dozens of Palestinians as it launched what it described as a "counter-terrorism" operation in the West Bank.
Overnight Sunday, Palestinian officials said Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques.
"With attacks by Israeli settlers, and the creation of settlements and outposts, hitting an all-time high, third states must act urgently and in unison to halt the continuing killing and dispossession of the Palestinian people, and to bring an end to the Israeli occupation," Shamdasani said.
The comments came after Ramiz Alakbarov, the UN's deputy special coordinator for the Middle East peace process, warned the UN Security Council on Tuesday that the situation in the West Bank was "rapidly deteriorating."
Since the start of the Gaza war, at least 1,097 Palestinians, including fighters, have been killed by Israeli troops or settlers, according to Palestinian figures.
Official Israeli data shows that at least 48 Israelis, civilians and security personnel, have been killed in attacks by Palestinians or during Israeli military operations.
Excluding annexed east Jerusalem, around three million Palestinians live in the West Bank alongside more than 500,000 Israelis residing in settlements that are illegal under international law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RXZ motorcycle gathering members warned not to flout the law
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RXZ Members motorcycle gathering participants who commit dangerous riding, reckless acts or traffic offences during may find the police at their doorsteps.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said police had prepared recording teams to monitor the convoy, with footage of offences to be reviewed before further action is taken.
"From the enforcement perspective, we will remain firm. Any offences committed by road users or RXZ Members, including dangerous riding, reckless actions or violations of the law, will be recorded.
"We already have recording teams prepared and we will record all incidents. The footage will be reviewed and action will be taken accordingly," he told reporters at federal police headquarters in Bukit Aman.
The RXZ Members motorcycle gathering will be held at the Gong Badak Motor Racing Circuit in Kuala Nerus, Terengganu, over two days starting Friday.
Hasbullah said the recordings would serve as evidence for police action against participants found breaching traffic laws.
"Do not be surprised if policemen come to your homes later to take action based on the recordings," he said.
He said police would also adopt an advocacy approach by engaging with organisers and participants to promote responsible road use.
Hasbullah said police had suggested that its personnel be involved in the programme to remind participants that roads were not meant to be used to display reckless behaviour or endanger other road users.
He said the RXZ Members gathering is a positive initiative that brings motorcycle enthusiasts together but stressed that roads must not be misused until other road users become victims.
"If the situation cannot be controlled and the risks outweigh the benefits, next year we will adopt a more aggressive approach," he said.
He added that the approach was not intended to stop the programme, but to deter dangerous behaviour and prevent innocent road users from becoming victims.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Nicky Liow gets DNAA in RM36mil money laundering case after tax settlement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Nicky Liow has been granted a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA) on 26 money laundering charges involving more than RM36 million after the prosecution withdrew the case.
His lawyer, Datuk Rajpal Singh, confirmed that the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) decided not to proceed with the prosecution after Liow, whose full name is Liow Soon Hee, settled RM400,000 in outstanding taxes with the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
"He was granted a DNAA. It was given in 2022," Rajpal said when contacted.
A DNAA releases an accused without a conviction but does not amount to an acquittal. The prosecution may revive the charges in the future if new evidence or circumstances justify doing so.
According to the charge sheets, Liow as a company director was allegedly involved in money laundering and possessing monies believed to be proceeds from unlawful activities.
He was accused of committing the offence in several places near the Klang Valley between 2016 and 2021.
The charges were framed under Section 4(1)(a) and 4(1)(b) Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act (AMLATFPUAA).
The offence under AMLATFPUAA carries a jail term not exceeding 15 years' and a fine of at least five times the sum obtained from money laundering or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
On April 9, 2021, Liow and his brother were charged in the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court for allegedly being members of an organised crime group.
Liow was charged in absentia, as he was on the run.
However, Liow voluntarily surrendered to the police on April 11, 2022. He was charged with 26 money laundering charges the next day.
On July 7, the same year, the Court of Appeal acquitted and discharged 14 accused, including Liow's two younger brothers from charges of being involved in the organised crime group.
This is after the A-GC had received representations from all appellants to be fully acquitted of the charges.
On July 24, 2023, Liow's younger brother Liow Wei Kin was also freed from tax evasion and money laundering charges after he paid RM4.147 million worth of unpaid taxes, special penalty, fine and compound for his money laundering charges.
Liow, who is the founder of Winner Dynasty Group, had been tracked down by the police over a Macau Scam syndicate after 68 of its members were arrested in "Op Pelican 3.0" in March 2021.
On April 26, the same year, the Pahang palace stripped Liow of the Darjah Kebesaran Darjah Sri Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (SSAP) which carries the title of Datuk Seri.
Liow recently made headlines after a photograph of him wearing a PKR shirt alongside party president and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim surfaced online, sparking speculation over the status of his court case.
On July 26, PKR secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh denied that Liow was a party member, saying there was no record of him having applied for membership.
Liow later told a press conference that the PKR Youth shirt he wore had been purchased at a charity event and did not indicate any affiliation with the party.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Myanmar agrees to take back 5,000 Rohingya from Malaysia
Article:
JELEBU: Myanmar has agreed to accept an initial group of 5,000 Rohingya from Malaysia following negotiations between the two governments, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the move was part of broader efforts to address the long-running Rohingya issue while maintaining public order in Malaysia.
"People ask why we do not simply send them back. Send them where? Myanmar had refused to accept them before.
"Now, because of our good relations with Myanmar, they have agreed to take back 5,000 from Malaysia," he said in a speech at the Majlis Minum Petang Bersama PMX in Simpang Durian.
Anwar said Myanmar was also taking back 300,000 Rohingya from Bangladesh, describing the development as the result of diplomatic negotiations.
Anwar said the government would continue to act firmly against Rohingya refugees who disrupted public spaces and traffic, stressing that Malaysia's laws must be respected.
"I have instructed the police and border authorities that I do not want Rohingya disrupting roads or public places. This is Malaysia and they cannot disturb public order.
"We will provide designated places for them to stay, but they must not interfere with Malaysians' businesses or traffic," he said.
He said calls by some quarters to simply deport the Rohingya ignored the reality that Myanmar had previously refused to receive them.
Anwar said maintaining good diplomatic relations with neighbouring countries was crucial to resolving such complex humanitarian issues through negotiations rather than rhetoric.
On Monday, hundreds of Rohingya refugees gathered outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Jalan Bukit Petaling here after allegedly being forced to leave their settlement in Penang.
All 113 Rohingya refugees were later relocated after undergoing overnight police screening and identity verification.
A total of 66 were relocated to Kuala Lumpur, 29 to Selangor and 18 to Penang
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Haji welcomes release of RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has welcomed the government's decision to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into its management.
"TH has already taken note of the RCI recommendations on what happened in the past prior to 2018. TH has since moved on," it said in a statement.
The pilgrims' fund board said it had already implemented 75 per cent of the report's recommendations, while the remaining measures were still in progress.
"TH has adopted and implemented 75 per cent of the RCI recommendations to improve the governance and wellbeing of the institution. The balance is currently work in progress," it said.
TH added that it had cleaned up its balance sheet, built up reserves and recorded its highest profit distribution rate in eight years.
The fund said the improvements had enabled it to raise profit distribution to 3.5 per cent, its highest rate in eight years, while maintaining hajj costs at RM33,300 per person for three consecutive years.
TH said it remained committed to protecting depositors' interests, strengthening public trust and ensuring the institution continued to operate with integrity and responsibility.
Earlier today, the cabinet agreed to declassify and release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Tabung Haji, ending years of speculation over findings into the pilgrims' fund's management between 2014 and 2020.
Government spokesman
Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil
said the decision was made after the cabinet received a briefing from Tabung Haji's top management and deliberated on the RCI findings.
He said the report would be made public today and would also be tabled and debated at a special Dewan Rakyat sitting in the near future.
The RCI was established in 2021 to investigate Tabung Haji's management and operations following concerns over its financial position, including an estimated RM11 billion gap between its assets and liabilities, as well as alleged breaches of the Tabung Haji Act.
Following the 2018 general election, government reviews found that Tabung Haji had RM70.3 billion in assets against RM74.4 billion in liabilities as at Dec 31, 2017.
The government also raised concerns that profit distributions had continued despite liabilities exceeding assets.
As part of efforts to restore the institution's financial position, underperforming assets were transferred to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd, a special-purpose vehicle wholly owned by the Minister of Finance Incorporated, under a restructuring exercise approved by the government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Making local a natural choice
Article:
LETTERS:
The government's effort to rebrand the four-decade-old 'Buy Malaysian Goods' campaign into 'Jom Beli Produk Malaysia' (Jom Malaysia) is a welcome move.
As an ongoing national effort, it also raises an important question - what will persuade consumers to continue choosing local in the long run?
The answer is simple; quality, value and trust.
Patriotism may encourage someone to try a local product for the first time, but it is the product itself that determines whether they will buy it again.
Consumers deserve products that are well made, competitively priced and capable of meeting the same standards as imported alternatives.
Fortunately, many Malaysian brands have already shown that this is possible.
From halal food and beauty products to fashion and household goods, local businesses have earned loyal customers by delivering quality, innovation and consistency.
Their success proves that Malaysian products can compete – not because they are local, but because they offer genuine value.
This is the direction we should continue to pursue. It should encourage businesses to keep improving their products while giving consumers more reasons to choose Malaysian products with confidence.
Choosing local aligns with Sustainable Development Goals like SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
It is about recognising that every purchase can reduce our reliance on global supply chains, sustain local businesses, create jobs and strengthen Malaysia's economy.
Apart from patriotic campaigns, the future of local products will also depend on whether Malaysian businesses continue to earn consumers' trust through quality, innovation and value.
When local products consistently meet those expectations, buying Malaysian products will no longer feel like an act of patriotism.
It will simply become the natural choice.
SAFIYYA AISYAH ABDULL HADI
Faculty of Communication and Media Studies
Universiti Teknologi MARA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zimbabwe explores media cooperation with Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zimbabwe is looking to forge media cooperation with Malaysia through a proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU), with talks at an advanced stage.
Zimbabwe's Permanent Secretary for Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services, Nick Mangwana, said most of the proposed MoU's provisions had already been agreed upon, paving the way for collaboration in digital transformation, broadcasting, news operations and professional exchanges during an official visit to Media Prima Berhad's News and Current Affairs division.
"Part of this journey is to build a collaborative relationship in the media sector between Malaysia and Zimbabwe and we are working on an MoU.
"Most of the clauses have already been agreed on how we can cooperate in the media space," he told reporters after the dialogue session today.
Accompanied by representatives from Zimbabwe's Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Ministry, Mangwana said the visit to Media Prima was part of the delegation's official programme in Malaysia to strengthen bilateral ties and explore collaboration between the two countries' media sectors.
The dialogue session focused on sharing best practices in digital transformation, broadcasting, newsroom operations, media innovation and capacity building, while exploring strategic partnerships and professional exchanges between Malaysian and Zimbabwean media organisations.
He said stronger media cooperation would complement existing diplomatic relations by fostering greater people-to-people understanding.
[[nid:1499733]]
"Even though we cooperate very well at a diplomatic level, if nobody is talking about it then our populations don't get to know about it.
"So now we just need our media to cooperate so that Malaysia doesn't become a strange country to Zimbabweans and, of course, Zimbabwe won't be a strange country to Malaysians," he said.
Mangwana said about 5,000 Malaysians visited Zimbabwe each year and expressed hope the figure would grow, highlighting attractions such as Victoria Falls and the country's renowned safari industry.
He also pointed to the long-standing education ties between the two countries, saying Zimbabwe had sent about 500 students to Malaysia annually for the past 17 years.
Following the dialogue session, the delegation was briefed by New Straits Times' group editor Farrah Naz Karim on NSTP's KLIK initiative, a digital archive facility containing more than 15 million documents, photographs and news articles dating back to its founding year of 1845.
Describing the visit as "a journey of discovery", Mangwana praised Media Prima for adapting to the rapidly evolving media landscape.
"They've been very nimble and creative in keeping legacy media relevant while embracing new technologies to ensure they are where the audience is.
"It was quite a journey of discovery for us. We have a lot of takeaways to take home and incorporate into our practices," he said.
Also present during the visit were New Straits Times deputy group editor Sharanjit Singh, Berita Harian group editor Zulkifli Jalil, Berita Harian deputy group editor M. Thillinadan, and Media Prima group Corporate Communications Department and Chairman's Office group general manager Azlan Abdul Aziz.

Title: NS polls: Fahmi warns against fake news on WhatsApp
Article:
SEREMBAN: The public has been urged to be wary of fake news related to the Negri Sembilan election, particularly content circulated via WhatsApp.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said his team had observed a surge in content being shared without links, consisting only of images and videos.
"Some of the information being shared comes without any supporting details. We do not know whether the images or videos being circulated are recent or old.
"Everyone must remain vigilant. If you receive any news that cannot be verified, check it immediately with mainstream media such as TV3, Berita Harian, the New Straits Times, Harian Metro, RTM and Awani," he said.
He said this after visiting Media Prima Bhd's command centre in conjunction with the Negri Sembilan election here today.
Present were Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer, Datuk Mohd Efendi Omar; TV3 News and Current Affairs Department editor, Halim Mohamed; and Berita Harian, senior news editor, Veena Rusli.
Fahmi said the public should verify whether official and mainstream media had reported the information being circulated.
"Journalists with mainstream media adhere to journalistic ethics and carry out their duties professionally.
"That is why fact verification and fact-checking are crucial. If you are unsure, do not share it, especially anything received through WhatsApp," he said.
On PH's campaign momentum, Fahmi said the coalition's candidates remained upbeat and were continuing with a strategy tailored to the state, which differed significantly from the approach used in Johor.
"In this election, we are placing greater emphasis on face-to-face campaigning by going door-to-door to engage voters in their homes and spend more quality time with them.
"Another difference is that Negri Sembilan has a smaller electorate than Johor. This allows our candidates to spend more quality time with voters," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] Suspended cop among 5 held as police seize RM21.3m in meth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A suspended police officer is believed to have masterminded a drug trafficking syndicate dealing in methamphetamine for both the local and international markets.
Federal Narcotic Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said five Malaysian men, aged 39 to 46, were arrested under Op Waja between Saturday and yesterday.
Police seized 425.3kg of methamphetamine that were packed into 410 plastic packets. The drugs are estimated to be worth RM21.3 million.
"The syndicate is believed to have been active since early this year and involved members from Kelantan.
"They used terrace houses in the Klang Valley as storage before distributing the drugs to the local market and overseas," Hussein said at the Cheras police headquarters today.
Checks revealed the suspended police officer has been off duty since 2024 and has one drug-related offence on his record.
Hussein said the five suspects have been remanded for six days from July 26 to facilitate investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
He said police had identified other members of the syndicate.
"Police will never compromise with any officer or personnel who betrays the force."

Title: Negri polls: Fahmi praises Media Prima election coverage operations
Article:
SEREMBAN: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil praised Media Prima Bhd's (MPB) performance, highlighting the company's professionalism in managing operations during the Negri Sembilan state election.
Fahmi said MPB had made effective use of its existing equipment while adopting new technology to help manage production costs throughout its election coverage.
"What Media Prima has demonstrated is quite impressive because, if we watch its television broadcasts or social media coverage, it is clearly professional.
"In terms of operations, I was informed that Media Prima is using new technology alongside its existing equipment, enabling production costs to be managed more efficiently.
"This is a significant improvement that is quite commendable without compromising production quality," he said.
He said this after visiting MPB's command centre for the Negri Sembilan state election here today.
Also present were Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer Datuk Mohd Effendi Omar, TV3 News and Current Affairs Department editor Halim Mohamed, and Berita Harian senior news editor Veena Rusli.
Fahmi said he was also briefed on several matters, including MPB's preparations for the upcoming Melaka state election.
"Although it has not yet been announced, Media Prima is already at a good level of preparedness.
"We will do our best to assist and address any issues that arise, including those related to internet connectivity," he said.
During the visit, he spent about 30 minutes meeting MPB media personnel involved in covering the state election.
"Today, I had the opportunity to see firsthand the operations centre for the Media Prima team here," he said.
He added that, so far, no Media Prima journalists had encountered any problems while carrying out their duties.
"If any media personnel face any issues, they can inform me directly or forward the information to the Malaysian Media Council," he said.
MPB is the country's largest integrated media company, operating major television channels, radio stations, print publications, and digital media platforms.
